Exploration of the New Hampshire Birth Cohort placenta data (GEO
**GSE71678**): CpG probe summaries and a self-organising map (SOM) of CpGs,
then SOM, t-SNE and UMAP embeddings of the placental metals with clusters
characterised by covariates.

Sources: `EnvBRAN/gwas_test.ipynb` ("GWAS – cpgs") and
`EnvBRAN/j_arrow.ipynb` ("Arrow with Julia", metals part). The `.md`
exports and figures were dropped.

```{julia}
using ExposomicsJulia
using DataFrames, Statistics, LinearAlgebra, Plots, StatsBase, CategoricalArrays
using GigaSOM, TSne, UMAP
```

Self-organizing maps (SOM) are a type of artificial neural network that use unsupervised learning to create a low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional data. The algorithm involves iteratively adjusting the weights of neurons in the network to create a topological map of the input data. The formula for SOM can be expressed as follows:

Let there be a set of input vectors X = {x1, x2, ..., xn} where each vector x has m features x = (x1, x2, ..., xm).
The goal of SOM is to create a map of k neurons arranged in a grid with topological structure. Each neuron j in the map has a weight vector wj = (w1j, w2j, ..., wmj) with the same dimension as the input vectors.

The algorithm works as follows:

1. Initialize the weights of the neurons randomly.

2. For each input vector xi, find the neuron j with the closest weight vector to xi. This is known as the Best Matching Unit (BMU) and can be calculated as follows: $$ BMU = argmin_{j} \Vert{x_i - w_j}\Vert $$ where ||.|| denotes the Euclidean distance.

3. Update the weights of the BMU and its neighbors in the map to move them closer to xi. This is done using the following formula: $$ w_{j}(t+1) = w_{j}(t) + \alpha(t)h_{j,i}(t)(x_i - w_{j}(t)) $$ where t is the iteration number, α(t) is the learning rate which decreases over time, and h_{j,i}(t) is the neighborhood function which determines the extent to which neighboring neurons are updated. It is defined as: $$ h_{j,i}(t) = exp\Bigg(-\frac{\Vert{r_i - r_j}\Vert^2}{2\sigma^2(t)}\Bigg) $$ where r_i and r_j are the positions of neurons i and j in the grid, and σ(t) is the neighborhood size which also decreases over time.

4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for a fixed number of iterations or until convergence. The resulting SOM can be used to visualize the high-dimensional data in a low-dimensional space and identify clusters or patterns in the data.

## CpG probes

```{julia}
#| eval: false
df   = read_arrow(datadir("GSE71678", "GSE71678_cov_original.arrow"));
cpgs = read_arrow(datadir("GSE71678", "GSE71678_cpgs_original.arrow"));
cpgs = cpgs[:, vcat("ID_REF", df.ID)];
x = Matrix{Float64}(cpgs[:, 2:end]);
size(x)
```

Per-probe mean, SD, range and number (and fraction) of distinct values:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
cpgs_stats = DataFrame(ID_REF = cpgs.ID_REF, mean = vec(mean(x, dims = 2)), sd = vec(std(x, dims = 2)),
                       min = vec(minimum(x, dims = 2)), max = vec(maximum(x, dims = 2)),
                       n_unique = [length(unique(r)) for r in eachrow(x)])
cpgs_stats.frac_unique = cpgs_stats.n_unique ./ size(x, 2);
```

Probe types (`cg` CpG sites and `ch.<chr>` non-CpG probes):

```{julia}
#| eval: false
println("cg   - ", sum(contains.(cpgs.ID_REF, "cg")))
for c in 1:9
    println("ch.$c - ", sum(contains.(cpgs.ID_REF, "ch.$c")))
end
```

SOM of the `ch.2` probes:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
txc1 = Matrix{Float64}(x[contains.(cpgs.ID_REF, "ch.2"), :]);
som = initGigaSOM(txc1, 20, 20)
som = trainGigaSOM(som, txc1)
mapToGigaSOM(som, txc1);
e = embedGigaSOM(som, txc1);
scatter(e[:, 1], e[:, 2], label = "", title = "SOM plot")
```

## Placental metals

```{julia}
#| eval: false
dfi = read_arrow(datadir("GSE71678", "GSE71678_cov_imputed.arrow"))
metals = names(dfi)[[8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16]]
Xm = Matrix{Float64}(dfi[:, metals]);
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
som = initGigaSOM(Xm, 20, 20)
som = trainGigaSOM(som, Xm)
e = embedGigaSOM(som, Xm);
scatter(e[:, 1], e[:, 2], title = "GigaSOM", label = "")

y_tsne = tsne(Xm, 2, 8, 1000, 30, pca_init = true, progress = false);
scatter(y_tsne[:, 1], y_tsne[:, 2], title = "Clusters T-Sne", label = "")

umap_model = UMAP.fit(permutedims(Xm), 2; n_epochs = 500).embedding
```

Colour the UMAP by birth-weight class (also available: preterm, sex,
maternal-age class):

```{julia}
#| eval: false
bw_class = cut(dfi[:, "birth weight (grams)"], [0, 2800, 3200, 3500, 3700, 4000, 10000])
countmap(bw_class)
col_preterm = dfi[:, "gestational age"] .< 37
col_gender  = dfi[:, "infant gender"] .== "Female"
col_mage    = cut(dfi[:, "maternal age"], [18, 27, 30, 32, 35, 37, 50])
scatter_embedding(umap_model; groups = string.(bw_class), title = "Clusters UMAP")
```

Characterise the left-most UMAP cluster:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
cluster_1 = umap_model[1, :] .< -3.8
countmap(dfi[cluster_1, "ever_smoker"])
describe(dfi[cluster_1, 1:22])
countmap(dfi[cluster_1, "mom_education"]), countmap(dfi[:, "mom_education"])
```
